sanskrit: rāghavas tv apayāteṣu tapasviṣu vicintayan na tatrārocayad vāsaṃ kāraṇair bahubhis tadā
english: When the ascetics had departed, Rāghava, reflecting upon many reasons, did not find it agreeable to remain there any longer.

sanskrit: iha me bharato dṛṣṭo mātaraś ca sanāgarāḥ sā ca me smṛtir anveti tān nityam anuśocataḥ
english: "Here Bharata saw me, and the mothers with all the townspeople — that memory follows me always, as I grieve for them continually."

sanskrit: skandhāvāraniveśena tena tasya mahātmanaḥ hayahastikarīṣaiś ca upamardaḥ kṛto bhṛśam
english: The encampment of that great-souled one's army, with the dung of horses and elephants, had greatly trampled and polluted the ground of this hermitage.

sanskrit: tasmād anyatra gacchāma iti saṃcintya rāghavaḥ prātiṣṭhata sa vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca saṃgataḥ
english: Having deliberated thus — "therefore let us go elsewhere" — Rāghava set out, accompanied by the daughter of Videha and by Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: so 'trer āśramam āsādya taṃ vavande mahāyaśāḥ taṃ cāpi bhagavān atriḥ putravat pratyapadyata
english: Reaching the hermitage of Atri, that greatly renowned one paid homage to him; and the blessed Atri in turn received him as a son.

sanskrit: svayam ātithyam ādiśya sarvam asya susatkṛtam saumitriṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ sītāṃ ca samasāntvayat
english: Having himself directed the hospitality so that everything was fittingly honoured for him, Atri also comforted the highly blessed Saumitri and Sītā.

sanskrit: patnīṃ ca tam anuprāptāṃ vṛddhām āmantrya satkṛtām sāntvayām āsa dharmajñaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: Addressing his aged wife who had come to meet them, and having honoured her well, that knower of dharma, who was devoted to the welfare of all beings, entreated her to comfort Sītā.

sanskrit: anasūyāṃ mahābhāgāṃ tāpasīṃ dharmacāriṇīm pratigṛhṇīṣva vaidehīm abravīd ṛṣisattamaḥ
english: The foremost among sages said: "Receive the daughter of Videha — Anasūyā, the greatly blessed female ascetic, the one who walks in dharma."

sanskrit: rāmāya cācacakṣe tāṃ tāpasīṃ dharmacāriṇīm daśa varṣāṇy anāvṛṣṭyā dagdhe loke nirantaram
english: He declared to Rāma concerning that female ascetic who walks in dharma: "When the world was scorched without respite by ten years of drought,

sanskrit: yayā mūlaphale sṛṣṭe jāhnavī ca pravartitā ugreṇa tapasā yuktā niyamaiś cāpy alaṃkṛtā
english: she, endowed with fierce austerity and adorned with religious vows, created roots and fruits and caused the Jāhnavī to flow.

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi yayā taptaṃ mahat tapaḥ anasūyāvratais tāta pratyūhāś ca nibarhitāḥ
english: By her the great austerity of ten thousand years was practised, dear one, and through the vows of Anasūyā all obstacles were destroyed.

sanskrit: devakāryanimittaṃ ca yayā saṃtvaramāṇayā daśarātraṃ kṛtvā rātriḥ seyaṃ māteva te 'nagha
english: She, acting swiftly for the sake of the gods' purpose, compressed ten nights into one night — she is like a mother to you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tām imāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ namaskāryāṃ yaśasvinīm abhigacchatu vaidehī vṛddhām akrodhanāṃ sadā
english: Let the daughter of Videha approach this venerable, illustrious one, who is worthy of reverence by all beings and who is ever free from anger."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ tathety uktvā sa rāghavaḥ sītām uvāca dharmajñām idaṃ vacanam uttamam
english: When the sage spoke thus, Rāghava replied "So be it" and then addressed these excellent words to Sītā, who knows dharma:

sanskrit: rājaputri śrutaṃ tv etan muner asya samīritam śreyo 'rtham ātmanaḥ śīghram abhigaccha tapasvinīm
english: "Princess, you have heard what this sage has said. For your own good, go quickly to that female ascetic.

sanskrit: anasūyeti yā loke karmabhiḥ kyātim āgatā tāṃ śīghram abhigaccha tvam abhigamyāṃ tapasvinīm
english: She who is known in the world as Anasūyā by virtue of her deeds — go quickly to that female ascetic, who is worthy of approach."

sanskrit: sītā tv etad vacaḥ śrutvā rāghavasya hitaiṣiṇī tām atripatnīṃ dharmajñām abhicakrāma maithilī
english: Hearing these words of Rāghava, who wished her well, the daughter of Mithilā, Sītā, approached that wife of Atri, the knower of dharma.

sanskrit: śithilāṃ valitāṃ vṛddhāṃ jarāpāṇḍuramūrdhajām satataṃ vepamānāṅgīṃ pravāte kadalī yathā
english: She was frail, wrinkled, and old, with hair whitened by age, her limbs trembling constantly like a plantain tree in the wind.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu sītā mahābhāgām anasūyāṃ pativratām abhyavādayad avyagrā svaṃ nāma samudāharat
english: Sītā, undisturbed, paid reverence to that greatly blessed Anasūyā, the devoted wife, and announced her own name.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca vaidehī tāpasīṃ tām aninditām baddhāñjalipuṭā hṛṣṭā paryapṛcchad anāmayam
english: And having paid homage, the daughter of Videha, with palms joined in a cupped gesture, delightedly enquired after the well-being of that blameless female ascetic.

sanskrit: tataḥ sītāṃ mahābhāgāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ dharmacāriṇīm sāntvayanty abravīd dhṛṣṭā diṣṭyā dharmam avekṣase
english: Then, seeing that greatly blessed Sītā, the one who walks in dharma, Anasūyā cheerfully spoke words of comfort: "By good fortune you regard dharma!

sanskrit: tyaktvā jñātijanaṃ sīte mānam ṛddhiṃ ca mānini avaruddhaṃ vane rāmaṃ diṣṭyā tvam anugacchasi
english: O Sītā, O noble lady, by good fortune you follow Rāma into the forest, giving up your kinsfolk, your pride, and your prosperity, though he is confined there.

sanskrit: nagarastho vanastho vā pāpo vā yadi vāśubhaḥ yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ
english: Whether dwelling in a city or in the forest, whether wicked or inauspicious — women for whom the husband is dear, their worlds are of great prosperity.

sanskrit: duḥśīlaḥ kāmavṛtto vā dhanair vā parivarjitaḥ strīṇām ārya svabhāvānāṃ paramaṃ daivataṃ patiḥ
english: Whether ill-natured, given over to desire, or destitute of wealth — the husband is the supreme deity for women of noble nature, O noble lady.

sanskrit: nāto viśiṣṭaṃ paśyāmi bāndhavaṃ vimṛśanty aham sarvatra yogyaṃ vaidehi tapaḥ kṛtam ivāvyayam
english: When I reflect, I see no kinsman more distinguished than this, O daughter of Videha — one fit in every way, like austerity performed that bears imperishable fruit.

sanskrit: na tv evam avagacchanti guṇa doṣam asat striyaḥ kāmavaktavyahṛdayā bhartṛnāthāś caranti yāḥ
english: But wicked women do not understand this distinction between virtue and fault — those who behave guided by their hearts' desires and idle talk, though their lord is the husband.

sanskrit: prāpnuvanty ayaśaś caiva dharmabhraṃśaṃ ca maithili akārya vaśam āpannāḥ striyo yāḥ khalu tad vidhāḥ
english: Women who are indeed of such a kind, having fallen under the sway of improper conduct, acquire infamy and fall from dharma, O daughter of Mithilā.

sanskrit: tvadvidhās tu guṇair yuktā dṛṣṭalokaparāvarāḥ striyaḥ svarge cariṣyanti yathā puṇyakṛtas tathā
english: But women endowed with virtues like yours, who perceive the higher and lower worlds, will move in heaven just as those who have performed meritorious deeds."

sanskrit: sā tv evam uktā vaidehī anasūyān asūyayā pratipūjya vaco mandaṃ pravaktum upacakrame
english: Thus addressed by Anasūyā, the daughter of Videha, honouring her words without jealousy, began to speak gently in reply:

sanskrit: naitad āścaryam āryāyā yan māṃ tvam anubhāṣase viditaṃ tu mamāpy etad yathā nāryāḥ patir guruḥ
english: "What you say to me, noble lady, is no wonder — for this too is known to me: how the husband is the teacher for a woman.

sanskrit: yady apy eṣa bhaved bhartā mamārye vṛttavarjitaḥ advaidham upavartavyas tathāpy eṣa mayā bhavet
english: Even if this husband of mine were devoid of proper conduct, O noble lady, he would nonetheless have to be served by me without duplicity.

sanskrit: kiṃ punar yo guṇaślāghyaḥ sānukrośo jitendriyaḥ sthirānurāgo dharmātmā mātṛvartī pitṛ priyaḥ
english: How much more so one who is praiseworthy for his virtues, compassionate, master of his senses, steadfast in affection, righteous in spirit, dutiful to his mothers, and beloved of his father.

sanskrit: yāṃ vṛttiṃ vartate rāmaḥ kausalyāyāṃ mahābalaḥ tām eva nṛpanārīṇām anyāsām api vartate
english: The same conduct that the mighty Rāma observes toward Kausalyā, he observes likewise toward the other queens and royal women.

sanskrit: sakṛd dṛṣṭāsv api strīṣu nṛpeṇa nṛpavatsalaḥ mātṛvad vartate vīro mānam utsṛjya dharmavit
english: Even toward women seen only once, that hero dear to kings, the knower of dharma, laying aside pride, conducts himself as toward a mother.

sanskrit: āgacchantyāś ca vijanaṃ vanam evaṃ bhayāvaham samāhitaṃ hi me śvaśrvā hṛdaye yat sthitaṃ mama
english: And coming to this lonely and dreadful forest, I hold within my heart what was collected and placed there by my mother-in-law.

sanskrit: prāṇipradānakāle ca yat purā tv agnisaṃnidhau anuśiṣṭā jananyāsmi vākyaṃ tad api me dhṛtam
english: And the words with which my mother instructed me formerly at the time of the giving of my hand, in the presence of the sacred fire — those words too are firmly held in my mind.

sanskrit: navīkṛtaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ vākyais te dharmacāriṇi patiśuśrūṣaṇān nāryās tapo nānyad vidhīyate
english: All of that has been renewed by your words, O one who walks in dharma. For a woman there is no austerity prescribed other than devoted service to her husband.

sanskrit: sāvitrī patiśuśrūṣāṃ kṛtvā svarge mahīyate tathā vṛttiś ca yātā tvaṃ patiśuśrūṣayā divam
english: Sāvitrī is honoured in heaven for having rendered devoted service to her husband, and in like manner you have gone to heaven through devoted service to your husband.

sanskrit: variṣṭhā sarvanārīṇām eṣā ca divi devatā rohiṇī ca vinā candraṃ muhūrtam api dṛśyate
english: She is the foremost among all women, and this goddess too in heaven — Rohiṇī is not seen even for a moment without the moon.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhāś ca pravarāḥ striyo bhartṛdṛḍhavratāḥ devaloke mahīyante puṇyena svena karmaṇā
english: And thus such eminent women, firm in their vow to their husbands, are honoured in the world of the gods by their own meritorious deeds."

sanskrit: tato 'nasūyā saṃhṛṣṭā śrutvoktaṃ sītayā vacaḥ śirasy āghrāya covāca maithilīṃ harṣayanty uta
english: Then Anasūyā, greatly delighted upon hearing Sītā's words, smelled her on the head and spoke, gladdening the daughter of Mithilā:

sanskrit: niyamair vividhair āptaṃ tapo hi mahad asti me tat saṃśritya balaṃ sīte chandaye tvāṃ śucivrate
english: "I possess great austerity acquired through various religious vows; relying on the power thereof, O Sītā, O one of pure observance, I desire to grant you a boon.

sanskrit: upapannaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca vacanaṃ tava maithili prītā cāsmy ucitaṃ kiṃ te karavāṇi bravīhi me kṛtam ity abravīt sītā tapobalasamanvitām
english: Your speech, O daughter of Mithilā, is fitting and proper; I am pleased — what fitting thing shall I do for you? Tell me" — thus Sītā spoke to her who was endowed with the power of austerity.

sanskrit: sā tv evam uktā dharmajñā tayā prītatarābhavat saphalaṃ ca praharṣaṃ te hanta sīte karomy aham
english: That knower of dharma, thus addressed by her, became even more pleased, and said: "Ah, O Sītā, I shall indeed make your delight bear fruit!

sanskrit: idaṃ divyaṃ varaṃ mālyaṃ vastram ābharaṇāni ca aṅgarāgaṃ ca vaidehi mahārham anulepanam
english: This excellent divine garland, this garment and ornaments, and this fragrant ointment, O daughter of Videha, this precious unguent —

sanskrit: mayā dattam idaṃ sīte tava gātrāṇi śobhayet anurūpam asaṃkliṣṭaṃ nityam eva bhaviṣyati
english: given by me, this shall adorn your limbs, O Sītā; suited to you, unstained, it will always remain so forever.

sanskrit: aṅgarāgeṇa divyena liptāṅgī janakātmaje śobhayiṣyāmi bhartāraṃ yathā śrīr viṣṇum avyayam
english: Anointed with the divine fragrant ointment, O daughter of Janaka, you will delight your husband as Śrī delights the eternal Viṣṇu."

sanskrit: sā vastram aṅgarāgaṃ ca bhūṣaṇāni srajas tathā maithilī pratijagrāha prītidānam anuttamam
english: The daughter of Mithilā accepted the garment, the fragrant ointment, the ornaments, and the garlands — that incomparable gift of affection.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tat sītā prītidānaṃ yaśasvinī śliṣṭāñjalipuṭā dhīrā samupāsta tapodhanām
english: Having received that gift of affection, the illustrious Sītā, steadfast, with hands joined and cupped together, sat beside that one whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: tathā sītām upāsīnām anasūyā dṛḍhavratā vacanaṃ praṣṭum ārebhe kathāṃ kāṃ cid anupriyām
english: Thus, with Sītā seated beside her, Anasūyā of firm vow began to ask a pleasing question:

sanskrit: svayaṃvare kila prāptā tvam anena yaśasvinā rāghaveṇeti me sīte kathā śrutim upāgatā
english: "I have heard the story, O Sītā, that you were won at the svayaṃvara by this illustrious Rāghava.

sanskrit: tāṃ kathāṃ śrotum icchāmi vistareṇa ca maithili yathānubhūtaṃ kārtsnyena tan me tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: I wish to hear that story in full, O daughter of Mithilā. You ought to tell me the whole of it as you experienced it."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā sītā tāṃ tato dharmacāriṇīm śrūyatām iti coktvā vai kathayām āsa tāṃ kathām
english: Thus addressed, Sītā said to that one who walks in dharma, "Listen then," and narrated the story:

sanskrit: mithilādhipatir vīro janako nāma dharmavit kṣatradharmaṇy abhirato nyāyataḥ śāsti medinīm
english: "The heroic Janaka by name, lord of Mithilā, a knower of dharma, devoted to the duties of the warrior order, rules the earth justly.

sanskrit: tasya lāṅgalahastasya karṣataḥ kṣetramaṇḍalam ahaṃ kilotthitā bhittvā jagatīṃ nṛpateḥ sutā
english: As he, plough in hand, was tilling the field-plot, I, they say, arose, cleaving the earth — the daughter of the king.

sanskrit: sa māṃ dṛṣṭvā narapatir muṣṭivikṣepatatparaḥ pāṃśu guṇṭhita sarvāṅgīṃ vismito janako 'bhavat
english: Seeing me, the king — intent on the throwing of clods — with all my limbs covered in dust, Janaka was astonished.

sanskrit: anapatyena ca snehād aṅkam āropya ca svayam mameyaṃ tanayety uktvā sneho mayi nipātitaḥ
english: Being childless, he took me with affection onto his own lap, saying "This is my daughter" — and his love fell upon me.

sanskrit: antarikṣe ca vāg uktāpratimā mānuṣī kila evam etan narapate dharmeṇa tanayā tava
english: And from the sky an incomparable, superhuman voice spoke: "Indeed so, O king — by dharma this is your daughter."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo dharmātmā pitā me mithilādhipaḥ avāpto vipulām ṛddhiṃ mām avāpya narādhipaḥ
english: Then my father, the righteous lord of Mithilā, greatly rejoiced, and that lord of men, having obtained me, attained great prosperity.

sanskrit: dattvā cāsmīṣṭavad devyai jyeṣṭhāyai puṇyakarmaṇā tayā saṃbhāvitā cāsmi snigdhayā mātṛsauhṛdāt
english: He entrusted me to his elder queen as one beloved, through her meritorious deeds, and I was honoured by her with tender maternal affection.

sanskrit: patisaṃyogasulabhaṃ vayo dṛṣṭvā tu me pitā cintām abhyagamad dīno vittanāśād ivādhanaḥ
english: But seeing that my marriageable age, easily attained through union with a husband, was at hand, my father fell into anxiety, helpless as a pauper at the loss of wealth.

sanskrit: sadṛśāc cāpakṛṣṭāc ca loke kanyāpitā janāt pradharṣaṇām avāpnoti śakreṇāpi samo bhuvi
english: The father of a maiden is subject to insult in the world from those of equal or inferior rank — even if he be equal to Indra on earth.

sanskrit: tāṃ dharṣaṇām adūrasthāṃ saṃdṛśyātmani pārthivaḥ cinntārṇavagataḥ pāraṃ nāsasādāplavo yatha
english: Seeing that insult as not far off and perceiving it within himself, the king, having entered the ocean of anxiety, could not reach the farther shore, like one without a boat.

sanskrit: ayonijāṃ hi māṃ jñātvā nādhyagacchat sa cintayan sadṛśaṃ cānurūpaṃ ca mahīpālaḥ patiṃ mama
english: For knowing me to be womb-unborn, that guardian of the earth, reflecting and reflecting, could not find a husband for me who was equal and fitting.

sanskrit: tasya buddhir iyaṃ jātā cintayānasya saṃtatam svayaṃ varaṃ tanūjāyāḥ kariṣyāmīti dhīmataḥ
english: This thought arose in that wise one, as he deliberated without cease: 'I shall conduct a svayaṃvara for my daughter.'

sanskrit: mahāyajñe tadā tasya varuṇena mahātmanā dattaṃ dhanurvaraṃ prītyā tūṇī cākṣayya sāyakau
english: At a great sacrifice, the great-souled Varuṇa had then given to him, with affection, an excellent bow and two inexhaustible quivers of arrows.

sanskrit: asaṃcālyaṃ manuṣyaiś ca yatnenāpi ca gauravāt tan na śaktā namayituṃ svapneṣv api narādhipāḥ
english: It was immovable by men, and even by great effort on account of its heaviness kings were unable to bend it even in their dreams.

sanskrit: tad dhanuḥ prāpya me pitrā vyāhṛtaṃ satyavādinā samavāye narendrāḥ pūrvam āmantrya pārthivān
english: Having obtained that bow, my truth-speaking father declared, first summoning the lords of men and kings together:

sanskrit: idaṃ ca dhanur udyamya sajyaṃ yaḥ kurute naraḥ tasya me duhitā bhāryā bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'The man who lifts this bow and strings it — his wife my daughter shall become, without doubt.'

sanskrit: tac ca dṛṣṭvā dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ gauravād girisaṃnibham abhivādya nṛpā jagmur aśaktās tasya tolane
english: And seeing that most excellent bow, mountainlike in its heaviness, the kings paid homage and departed, unable to lift it.

sanskrit: sudīrghasya tu kālasya rāghavo 'yaṃ mahādyutiḥ viśvāmitreṇa sahito yajñaṃ draṣṭuṃ samāgataḥ
english: But after a very long time, this Rāghava of great splendour came to behold the sacrifice, accompanied by Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ viśvāmitras tu dharmātmā mama pitrā supūjitaḥ
english: Rāma of truly heroic prowess came with his brother Lakṣmaṇa; and the righteous Viśvāmitra was fittingly honoured by my father.

sanskrit: provāca pitaraṃ tatra rāghavo rāmalakṣmaṇau sutau daśarathasyemau dhanurdarśanakāṅkṣiṇau ity uktas tena vipreṇa tad dhanuḥ samupānayat
english: He spoke to my father there: 'These two sons of Daśaratha, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are desirous of beholding the bow.' Addressed thus by that brahmin, my father caused the bow to be brought forth.

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tad ānamya sa vīryavān jyāṃ samāropya jhaṭiti pūrayām āsa vīryavān
english: In a mere instant that mighty one bent it, and with a swift motion strung the bowstring — that mighty one fully drew it.

sanskrit: tena pūrayatā vegān madhye bhagnaṃ dvidhā dhanuḥ tasya śabdo 'bhavad bhīmaḥ patitasyāśaner iva
english: As he drew it forcefully, the bow broke in two in the middle; its sound was dreadful, like that of a falling thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tatra rāmāya pitrā satyābhisaṃdhinā udyatā dātum udyamya jalabhājanam uttamam
english: Then I was there being offered in bestowal to Rāma by my father, true to his word, who took up the excellent vessel of water.

sanskrit: dīyamānāṃ na tu tadā pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ avijñāya pituś chandam ayodhyādhipateḥ prabhoḥ
english: But Rāghava did not accept me as I was being given, not having learned the wish of his father, the lord and master of Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: tataḥ śvaśuram āmantrya vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam mama pitrā ahaṃ dattā rāmāya viditātmane
english: Then, having invited the aged king Daśaratha as father-in-law, I was given by my father to Rāma, the knower of the self.

sanskrit: mama caivānujā sādhvī ūrmilā priyadarśanā bhāryārthe lakṣmaṇasyāpi dattā pitrā mama svayam
english: And my younger sister, the virtuous and beautiful Ūrmilā, was also given by my father himself to Lakṣmaṇa as wife.

sanskrit: evaṃ dattāsmi rāmāya tadā tasmin svayaṃ vare anuraktā ca dharmeṇa patiṃ vīryavatāṃ varam
english: Thus was I given to Rāma at that svayaṃvara, and by dharma I am devoted to that husband, the best among the mighty."

sanskrit: anasūyā tu dharmajñā śrutvā tāṃ mahatīṃ kathām paryaṣvajata bāhubhyāṃ śirasy āghrāya maithilīm
english: Anasūyā, the knower of dharma, having heard that great story, embraced the daughter of Mithilā with both arms and smelled her on the head.

sanskrit: vyaktākṣarapadaṃ citraṃ bhāṣitaṃ madhuraṃ tvayā yathā svayaṃvaraṃ vṛttaṃ tat sarvaṃ hi śrutaṃ mayā
english: "Your speech has been clear of syllable and word, wonderful, sweet — the whole of how the svayaṃvara transpired has been heard by me.

sanskrit: rame 'haṃ kathayā te tu dṛḍhaṃ madhurabhāṣiṇi ravir astaṃ gataḥ śrīmān upohya rajanīṃ śivām
english: I indeed delight greatly in your story, O sweet-spoken one; the glorious sun has set, having brought on the auspicious night.

sanskrit: divasaṃ prati kīrṇānām āhārārthaṃ patatriṇām saṃdhyākāle nilīnānāṃ nidrārthaṃ śrūyate dhvaniḥ
english: The birds that scatter abroad each day in search of food — at twilight, having settled for sleep, their calls are heard.

sanskrit: ete cāpy abhiṣekārdrā munayaḥ phalaśodhanāḥ sahitā upavartante salilāplutavalkalāḥ
english: These sages too, wet from their ablutions, having purified their fruits, come together, their bark garments drenched with water.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām agnihotreṣu huteṣu vidhipurvakam kapotāṅgāruṇo dhūmo dṛśyate pavanoddhataḥ
english: From the oblation-fires of the sages, after the ritual offerings have been made, smoke the colour of a dove's wing is seen, lifted by the wind.

sanskrit: alpaparṇā hi taravo ghanībhūtāḥ samantataḥ viprakṛṣṭe 'pi ye deśe na prakāśanti vai diśaḥ
english: The trees, sparse-leafed yet dense in their mass on all sides, even at a distance make the directions invisible.

sanskrit: rajanī rasasattvāni pracaranti samantataḥ tapovanamṛgā hy ete veditīrtheṣu śerate
english: Creatures of the night's essence move about on all sides; and these animals of the ascetic grove lie down at the banks of the sacrificial altar.

sanskrit: saṃpravṛttā niśā sīte nakṣatrasamalaṃkṛtā jyotsnā prāvaraṇaś candro dṛśyate 'bhyudito 'mbare
english: Night has set in, O Sītā, adorned with constellations; the moon, wrapped in its own moonlight, is seen having risen in the sky.

sanskrit: gamyatām anujānāmi rāmasyānucarī bhava kathayantyā hi madhuraṃ tvayāhaṃ paritoṣitā
english: Go — I give you leave; be the companion of Rāma. I have been fully satisfied by you as you spoke so sweetly.

sanskrit: alaṃkuru ca tāvat tvaṃ pratyakṣaṃ mama maithili prītiṃ janaya me vatsa divyālaṃkāraśobhinī
english: And do adorn yourself now before my very eyes, O daughter of Mithilā — bring me joy, dear child, shining with the divine ornaments."

sanskrit: sā tadā samalaṃkṛtya sītā surasutopamā praṇamya śirasā tasyai rāmaṃ tv abhimukhī yayau
english: Then Sītā, having adorned herself, she who is like a daughter of the gods, bowed her head to Anasūyā and went toward Rāma.

sanskrit: tathā tu bhūṣitāṃ sītāṃ dadarśa vadatāṃ varaḥ rāghavaḥ prītidānena tapasvinyā jaharṣa ca
english: The best among the eloquent, Rāghava, beheld Sītā thus adorned and rejoiced at the gift of affection from the female ascetic.

sanskrit: nyavedayat tataḥ sarvaṃ sītā rāmāya maithilī prītidānaṃ tapasvinyā vasanābharaṇasrajām
english: Then the daughter of Mithilā, Sītā, reported to Rāma all the gift of affection from the female ascetic — the garment, ornaments, and garlands.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭas tv abhavad rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahārathaḥ maithilyāḥ satkriyāṃ dṛṣṭvā mānuṣeṣu sudurlabhām
english: Rāma and the great warrior Lakṣmaṇa were overjoyed upon seeing the honour rendered to the daughter of Mithilā — something exceedingly rare among humans.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ sarvarīṃ prītaḥ puṇyāṃ śaśinibhānanaḥ arcitas tāpasaiḥ siddhair uvāsa raghunandanaḥ
english: Then, pleased, that moon-faced joy of the Raghu line passed that auspicious night there, honoured by the siddha ascetics.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyām abhiṣicya hutāgnikān āpṛcchetāṃ naravyāghrau tāpasān vanagocarān
english: When that night had passed and the sacred fires had been anointed and the offerings made, those two tigers among men took leave of the ascetics who ranged the forest.

sanskrit: tāv ūcus te vanacarās tāpasā dharmacāriṇaḥ vanasya tasya saṃcāraṃ rākṣasaiḥ samabhiplutam
english: Those forest-ranging ascetics, walkers in dharma, spoke to them of the passage through that forest, which was beset by rākṣasas.

sanskrit: eṣa panthā maharṣīṇāṃ phalāny āharatāṃ vane anena tu vanaṃ durgaṃ gantuṃ rāghava te kṣamam
english: "This is the path of the great sages who fetch fruits in the forest; by this path, O Rāghava, it is fitting for you to enter the difficult forest."

sanskrit: itīva taiḥ prāñjalibhis tapasvibhir dvijaiḥ kṛtasvastyayanaḥ paraṃtapaḥ vanaṃ sabhāryaḥ praviveśa rāghavaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ sūrya ivābhramaṇḍalam
english: Thus, blessed by those ascetic brahmins with joined palms who had performed the rite of benediction, that scorcher of foes, Rāghava, with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa, entered the forest like the sun entering a mass of clouds.
